pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Graduation: First Steps is a Starter of a different kind. It is a short walk, not a lesson. You have been through The Basics; now the helpers who led those Starters are on the balcony, Doc Leo is on the stage, and your honors are on the lectern.

It takes a couple of minutes. Play it first, then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below.

There are two levels. First you cross campus to the hall, with a few small nods to lessons you took on the way. Then you walk the aisle to the stage.

The keys

Left and Right walk, Space hops, and Up and Down climb a ladder. There is nothing to fight and nothing that hurts. Walk into the scroll on the lectern and the game ends with your honors.

pages.head: Level 1: The Lab Yard
pages.html:
Level 1: The Lab Yard

Cross the yard to the lab doors. You start on the path with a welcome sign beside you, and the hall's doors are at the far end. Along the way are 3 small moments. Each one is a nod to a Starter you took in this stage, and each has a sign that gives its course number. Nothing here hurts, and nothing can trap you: every climb has a way back down.

  • Course 501, Switches. A lever on the path opens the gate in the wall beyond it.
  • Course 502, Three Tokens. Three tokens lie on the path; the gate beyond wants all three.
  • Course 504, Looks Like a Wall. A wall drawn like brick that you can simply walk through.

Walk through the doors under the banner to go inside.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How the arrival is made

  • The path. Open arrive.map in the map editor. The path is a row of solid paving blocks over two rows of dirt. The trees, banner poles and the hall's front are plain blocks you walk in front of; the hedge at each end is solid. This level has its own block set, arrive.bbl, beside the hall's grad.bbl: open grad.gam in the scenes editor and look at the block slot of each scene.
  • Course 501, Switches. The lever adds one to counter 22 and becomes leverOn (its handle flipped over). The powerGate takes one from counter 22 when touched, so after the lever it becomes sky.
  • Course 502, Three Tokens. Each token adds one to counter 21. The tokenGate takes three from it, so it opens only once all three are in your pocket.
  • Course 504, Looks Like a Wall. fakeBrick is a copy of the brick picture with nothing solid about it. Only the Blocks tab's rules tell the two apart.

pages.head: Level 2: The Aisle
pages.html:
Level 2: The Aisle

You start in the doorway at the back of the hall. Four signs along the red carpet say what is going on: WALK UP TO THE STAGE, YOUR HELPERS ARE HERE, THEY CHEER FOR YOU and DOC LEO HAS A SCROLL FOR YOU. Up on the balcony the eight helpers of The Basics wave and blink, each out of step with the others. Doc Leo waits beside the lectern, under the banner.

Walk up the carpet and onto the stage. The rolled-up scroll on the lectern is worth a hundred points, and touching it takes you to the ending.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How the aisle is made

  • The hall. Open hall.map in the map editor. The wall is the plain sky block. The floor is a row of carpet blocks, then stage blocks; two rows of subfloor sit under both. The two ends of the hall are the solid curtainEdge block, so you cannot walk out.
  • The crowd. Each helper is a ring of three blocks (hall.mia.0, .1 and .2, and so on) in grad.bbl: smiling, hands up, then a blink. Open a block in the blocks editor, and on its Animation tab you will see the Next block and the Time. Each helper has different times, so no two cheer together. A crowd that moves in step looks like a machine.
  • One drawing, many people. All eight are the hero's head, painted again in other skin, hair and beanie colors. In the editor you can do the same by copying a block and recoloring it. The Starters' Cast page lists the helpers.
  • Doc Leo. Two blocks, one over the other, standing on the stage. His top block is a ring like the helpers' (standing, grinning, blinking).
  • The scroll. The scroll block is the lectern's top with the scroll on it. Its Score points are 100 and Becomes block is lecternTop, the same lectern without the scroll. A scene link at the lectern joins it to the ending: open grad.gam in the scenes editor and look at the links of The Aisle.
  • The banner. Four ordinary blocks side by side with the words drawn in them, hung on the wall with no posts. The signs along the carpet are the same, with posts.

pages.head: What the honors mean
pages.html:
What the honors mean

A graduation comes after a group of Starters and gives you honors for what they taught. Honors in First Steps is for The Basics:

  • First Steps: walking, jumping, gravity and ladders.
  • Keys and Doors and Room to Room: keys, doors and getting from one room to the next.
  • Meet the Monsters and Watch Your Step: things that move and things that hurt.
  • Coins and Score: pickups that give points.
  • Smash It and Dig It: blocks that break and soil that turns into a tunnel.
  • Seeds and Nests: blocks that hatch things.

You do not have to finish every one. The graduation opens when you have finished most of them.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

  • A DOS game cannot ask your name, so the honors here do not have one. It says what you did.
  • The crowd cheers all the time. A block's animation runs on its own clock; it cannot wait until you walk past.
  • A block's loop is the same everywhere it is on the map, so every cell of one helper's block blinks together. Each helper is one cell here, so that does not show.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

  • Change the words on a sign, or the banner, in the blocks editor.
  • Change a helper's Time to make the crowd cheer in step. Does it look better or worse?
  • Draw a new person in the hall.mia blocks and put them in the hall.
  • Move the lectern, or put a second scroll on the stage.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
